meaning_fix: thing / matter / task / piece of business
reasoning: شغلة is the everyday word for a thing, matter or task, and it can also mean a job. 'Chore' is too narrow, since a household chore is more often shughl il-beet. Taa marbuta after ل is e.
This is a formal, written-style phrase, and the English says so. In conversation a Ramallah speaker says masalan. I kept th in mithaal because the phrase is formal, though some speakers say s or t.
The diphthong is monophthongised to long ee, giving beet (the scheme contrasts it with biit). It is written with kasra and ya, like كِيف. The word covers both house and home.
Palestinian dual of marra is marrteen, with the dual ending -een and no vowel between rr and t. MSA marratayn is not used.
Standard warm welcome to a man; فيك is the masculine singular 'you'. ح in مرحبا is 7, and ه in أهلا is h. The linking wa could also be reduced to u in fast speech.
Levantine for lip is shiffe, with the ف doubled, and the plural is shfaaf. The MSA shafa is not what is said. Taa marbuta after ف is e.
Maternal aunt's son. Word-initial hamza is a vowel seat, so it is written i with no glottal stop. Taa marbuta after ل is e. In use it usually takes a possessive, as in ibn khaalti.
Urban Palestinian merges ظ with ض, so ظهر is Duhur, and il- assimilates to it as iD-. I respelled ظ as ض to match what is said. Long oo in yoom.

ميدان (maydaan) is understood, but it is more typical of Syrian and Egyptian usage. In Palestine a public square is usually sa7a (ساحة), and a roundabout is duwwaar. The vowel is long ee from the old ay.

ذ is d in Palestinian speech, as in ma3duur, so I respelled it as د. The fu3l pattern takes a helping vowel, giving 3udur. Some speakers may say 3uzur in a more formal register, so I am not fully sure.
Form II passive participle with the prefix m- and no vowel before ح, giving m7ammaS. Final ص is emphatic, so S. Used for roasted nuts and seeds.
An everyday word, so ق is a glottal stop. Taa marbuta after ل is e. In fast speech the nb may sound like mb.
بقديش is the Palestinian 'how much is', with ق as a glottal stop and a doubled d. The hamza of إيجار is written after il-. ب plus ال assimilates to bish-shahr.
The -an adverb is MSA in origin but used in educated conversation. The colloquial alternatives are naadir ma + verb and 'aliil ma. Tanween is pronounced -an.
ثانية is taanye, with ث respelled as ت, as in the model تَالِت. Taa marbuta after ي is e. A natural spoken connector.
Palestinian says tilifoon for phone, with the possessive -i. ضاع is 'got lost', and ض is D.
كيف is keef. The hamza of أولاد is written after il- because it is inside a token. The question mark is not romanized.
Common Palestinian word for table, with emphatic T. Taa marbuta after ل is e.
Everyday phrase meaning long ago or for a long time. Long aa in zamaan.
The past tense of 'I grew up' is kbirt, with the first vowel dropped. The phrase means 'the older I got' or 'every time I grew up'.
The fi3l noun takes a helping vowel before the final consonant in speech, giving ribi7. ح is 7.
The possessive -o is Palestinian, not MSA -hu. Literally 'God have mercy on its days', said nostalgically about the past. The English gloss is a fair equivalent.

Religious proper name, so ق keeps [q] under the scheme. Some speakers say il-'iyaame. In the construct state كنيسة becomes kniisit. The Arabic name literally means 'Church of the Resurrection', and the English is the standard equivalent.
The city name Jenin, with a short i in the first syllable and long ii in the second.
ليلة is leele, and in the construct state it is leelt or leelit before imbaari7, the Palestinian form of yesterday. The phrase means last night.
